'''Rollie Tesh''' is a game designer credited as a designer of Decipher's ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game (SWCCG).<ref name="wp-swccg">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia (designer credit line)</ref>

== Name note ==

Wikipedia's SWCCG and Tom Braunlich articles use '''Rollie Tesh'''.<ref name="wp-swccg" /><ref name="wp-braunlich">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Braunlich Tom Braunlich], Wikipedia</ref> Some Decipher-era audio indexes and fandom mirrors use close spelling variants. This wiki uses '''Rollie Tesh''' to match Wikipedia's SWCCG designer line.

== SWCCG role ==

Wikipedia lists Tesh among SWCCG's designers with [[Tom Braunlich]], [[Warren Holland]], and [[Jerry Darcy]].<ref name="wp-swccg" /> With Braunlich, Tesh co-originated Decipher's licensed collectible-card-game approach and co-designed ''Star Trek: The Next Generation'' CCG before SWCCG.<ref name="wp-braunlich" /><ref name="wp-decipher">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decipher,_Inc. Decipher, Inc.], Wikipedia</ref>

Former Decipher staffer [[Mark Tuttle]] called SWCCG "Tom and Rollie's &hellip; game."<ref name="fantha">[https://www.fanthatracks.com/interviews/guest-interview-mark-tuttle/ Guest Interview: Mark Tuttle], Fantha Tracks, 15 March 2018</ref> Decipher's contemporary [[Radio Free Decipher]] series included episodes with Tesh and Braunlich billed as game creators.<ref name="rfd">[https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Radio_Free_Decipher Radio Free Decipher episode index], LOTR-TCG PC wiki</ref> The GeoCities anagram table unscrambles [[Elis Helrot]] as Rollie Tesh.<ref name="ana">[https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/anagrams.html Anagramed Decipherians]</ref>

== ''Pente'' and Decipher contact ==

Tesh and Braunlich were world champions of ''Pente'', a game later marketed by Decipher.<ref name="wp-braunlich" /><ref name="wp-decipher" /> In November 1993 they approached Decipher with a media-license CCG concept, leading to the ''Star Trek'' CCG (1994) and then SWCCG (December 1995).<ref name="wp-decipher" /><ref name="st-timeline">[https://web.archive.org/web/20080821113824/http://decipher.com/content/2004/st10/sttimeline.html The History of Star Trek CCG: The Timeline], Kathy McCracken, Decipher (Wayback)</ref>

''Pente'' sources also credit Tesh with proposing the Keryo-Pente variant while world champion; that abstract-game work is outside SWCCG scope but helps identify the same designer.<ref name="wp-pente">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pente Pente], Wikipedia</ref>
